transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess… my eating’s gotten a little out of hand. It started as just trying to eat cleaner for the lieutenant track, but now I’m cutting meals way down—like black coffee, a protein shake, maybe a small dinner. Even on shift days when I know I’m burning a lot more than that.
Have you ever made yourself vomit or used laxatives, diuretics, or diet pills to control your weight or the shape of your body?
No… I haven’t done that stuff. Not vomiting or pills or anything like that.
Have you been overly worried about your weight or the shape of your body lately?

Yeah… I guess I have been. I don’t really like saying that, but before work I’ll check the mirror and get stuck on whether my waist or my face look… sharp enough, I guess. If they don’t, it kind of throws me off and I don’t feel as ready or confident going in.
Do you ever feel like certain foods are off-limits or that eating a normal amount would cause you to gain weight in a way that feels unacceptable to you?

Yeah… kind of. Like if we have a big meal at the station, or even if I’ve just had more water, and the scale’s up a pound, I get this… tight feeling. Like I messed up, and everyone’s gonna notice I’m getting soft or don’t have control.
Have these concerns about your weight or eating habits started affecting your work, relationships, or other important areas of your life?

A little, I guess. I’m still doing my job fine, but… I’ve been skipping out on station meals more. When the crew orders food I’ll kind of keep to myself instead of joining in, so I’m probably not as much part of things as I used to be.
Have you noticed these concerns about your eating, weight, or body shape happening almost every day, or do they come and go?
I don’t know… it kind of comes and goes, I guess. I notice it more on some days than others.
Would you say your concerns about eating, weight, or your body shape happen almost every day, or are there significant periods where you don’t feel this way?
I’m not really sure. It’s not like I’m tracking it that way. Some days it’s there more, some days I can kind of ignore it. I don’t know if I’d say almost every day.
Would you say that your concerns about eating, weight, or your body shape happen on most days, even if they vary in how strong they feel?
Maybe… yeah, probably most days if I’m being honest. It’s not always loud or anything, but it’s kind of there in the background.
Do you have a strong fear of gaining weight or becoming fat, even if it's just a small amount?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t like saying it that way, but yeah. If the scale’s up even a pound after a big meal at the station or just water or whatever, I get this tight panicky feeling, like I messed up… like people are gonna notice and think I’m soft or out of control.
Can you describe how your concerns about weight or body shape have influenced what or how much you eat on a typical day?

I guess it started as just trying to eat cleaner, you know, for the lieutenant track and staying in shape. But now on a normal day it’s… pretty cut down.

Like I’ll have black coffee, maybe a protein shake, and then a small dinner. Even on shift days, when I know I’ve burned way more than that. I don’t really like admitting that, but yeah, it’s affecting how much I let myself eat.
When you look in the mirror, do you see yourself as bigger or heavier than you actually are, or do you feel like you need to lose weight even if others might not see you that way?

Yeah… I guess. Before work especially, I’ll check the mirror and I kind of lock onto my waist or my face, like whether I look… sharp enough, I guess. If I don’t, it throws me off. Makes me feel less confident going in.
Would you say that your concerns about eating, weight, or your body shape happen on most days, even if they vary in how strong they feel?

Yeah… most days, I’d say. It’s worse before work. I’ll check the mirror and get stuck on my waist or my face, like whether I look sharp enough. If I don’t, it kind of messes with my confidence going in… like I don’t feel as command-ready.
